content: Terbinafine is a medication prescribed to treat fungal infections affecting the toenails and fingernails. It belongs to a class of drugs known as antifungals, and it works by inhibiting the growth of fungi. Terbinafine is available in tablet form and is taken orally. For fingernail fungal infections, it is typically taken once daily for six weeks. For toenail fungal infections, it is usually taken once daily for 12 weeks. It is important to follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully. If you have any questions, consult your doctor or pharmacist. Take terbinafine exactly as directed and do not take more or less than prescribed. It may take several months after completing the medication for the fungal infection to be fully cured, as healthy nails need time to grow back. This medication may also be prescribed for other uses. If you have questions about its use for other conditions, consult your doctor or pharmacist. Before taking terbinafine, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to terbinafine or any other medications. Provide a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription medications, vitamins, nutritional supplements, and herbal products you are taking. Be sure to mention anticoagulants (e.g., warfarin), antidepressants (e.g., amitriptyline, nortriptyline), beta-blockers (e.g., atenolol, propranolol), cimetidine, immune-suppressing medications (e.g., cyclosporine, methotrexate), rifampin, and selegiline. Your doctor may need to adjust your medication doses or monitor you for side effects. Inform your doctor if you have a history of kidney or liver disease, HIV, or AIDS. Additionally, let your doctor know if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. If you become pregnant while taking terbinafine, contact your doctor immediately. You should not take terbinafine while breastfeeding. Unless otherwise instructed by your doctor, you can continue your normal diet while taking this medication. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not take a double dose to make up for a missed one. Terbinafine may cause side effects. Mild side effects include diarrhea, upset stomach, stomach pain, rash, itching, hives, and changes in or loss of taste. If these symptoms are severe or persistent, inform your doctor. Serious side effects are rare but require immediate medical attention. These include persistent upset stomach, loss of appetite, extreme fatigue, vomiting, pain in the upper right abdomen, dark urine, pale stools, severe or worsening skin rash, fever, sore throat, or other signs of infection. If you experience any unusual problems while taking this medication, contact your doctor. Serious side effects can also be reported to the FDA’s MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program. Store terbinafine in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture (do not store it in the bathroom). Dispose of expired or unneeded medication properly by consulting your pharmacist. In case of an overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual collapses or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. Keep all appointments with your doctor and laboratory, as certain tests may be ordered to monitor your response to terbinafine. Do not share this medication with others. If you have questions about refilling your prescription, consult your pharmacist.
